negative_findings.description: Searched in Montenegrin and English for a dedicated financial ombudsman / alternative dispute resolution body for banking and payments in Montenegro (terms: finansijski ombudsman, ombudsman za bankarske usluge, vansudsko rješavanje sporova korisnika finansijskih usluga).
negative_findings.result_summary: No dedicated financial ombudsman was found. The general human-rights Ombudsman (Zaštitnik ljudskih prava i sloboda) has no banking-specific mandate and explicitly no jurisdiction over courts; complaint escalation instead runs bank internal complaint body -> CBCG Service for the Protection of Users of Financial Services.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Rules out a source class that exists in neighbouring markets and concentrates complaint-channel collection on CBCG plus the consumer NGO CEZAP; also means no published individual complaint decisions naming banks.

negative_findings.description: Searched (sr and en) for an interchange-fee or card-scheme dispute, court case or competition proceeding in Montenegro (interchange naknada spor, međubankarska naknada, Visa, Mastercard, sudski postupak).
negative_findings.result_summary: No dispute, AZZK case or judgment on interchange was located. Only the statutory framework surfaced — a Law on interbank fees and special rules for payment card operations reported as Official Gazette of Montenegro no. 145/21 — plus bank card tariff PDFs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The adversarial payments-economics detail this cell is meant to harvest appears not to exist yet in Montenegro; card economics must instead be reconstructed from the statute, bank tariff sheets and CBCG fee-comparability disclosures.

negative_findings.description: Attempted to find a standalone published CBCG annual report on consumer/user protection with complaint counts by bank.
negative_findings.result_summary: CBCG pages state that data on complaints, their merit and measures taken are compiled and that a bylaw sets reporting deadlines, and the CBCG Annual Report contains a consumer-protection chapter, but no separate per-bank complaint statistics report URL was found in this pass. Unverified whether such a standalone publication exists.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Per-institution complaint counts are the highest-value item in this cell; if unpublished, an access-to-information request (slobodan pristup informacijama) may be the only route.

negative_findings.description: Searched for AZZK decisions specifically concerning Montenegrin banks or payment institutions.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank-related material found on azzk.me is largely cross-border (e.g. an older Societe Generale Banka Srbije / KBC Banka Beograd concentration PDF) and 2024 lists reportedly include NLB/Addiko and Alta Pay Group/Addiko items, but no domestic Montenegrin bank merger decision text was directly opened and confirmed in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The volume of genuinely Montenegro-specific banking merger decisions may be small; expectations for this channel should be calibrated before building heavy collection.

negative_findings.description: Court decision databases on sudovi.me were identified but their search/filter capabilities and full-text coverage for competition and banking matters were not exercised in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Listing URLs exist (/uscg/odluke/, /sdvi/odluke, /pscg) but it is unverified whether decisions are full-text searchable, anonymised, or only partially published.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines whether court/enforcement notices can be systematically collected or only sampled.

brief: Montenegro's complaint/enforcement channel rests on two publishing institutions: the Agency for Protection of Competition (AZZK, azzk.me), which posts full-text merger, cartel and dominance decisions plus sectoral analyses as PDFs, and the Central Bank (CBCG), whose Service for the Protection of Users of Financial Services handles complaint escalation and publishes fee-comparability data, complaint reporting bylaws and an annual consumer-protection chapter. Judicial review and commercial litigation are reachable through the sudovi.me court portal (Upravni sud for challenges to AZZK/CBCG acts, Privredni sud for bank disputes and insolvency), supplemented by the market inspectorate's annual reports on gov.me and the consumer NGO CEZAP as an early-warning layer. Two structural weaknesses stand out: there is no dedicated financial ombudsman, and no interchange or card-fee dispute could be found, so payments economics must be reconstructed from the 2021 interbank-fee law, bank tariff sheets and CBCG fee disclosures rather than from adversarial proceedings. Per-institution complaint statistics appear to be collected but not published, making a freedom-of-information request to CBCG the highest-value next action.
